author: WCIA
title: Salt Fork football hoping to continue consistent success - NewsBreak
text:
1 hours ago
CATLIN, Ill. (WCIA) - Salt Fork football has been a consistent contender in the Vermilion Valley Conference for many years.
The Storm has made a postseason appearance in each of the last 10 seasons, excluding the 2020 season which was canceled due to COVID.
The success translated from Brian Plotner to Joe Hageman in 2019, and again continued when Les Siefert took over as head coach in 2025. The Storm finished 5-5 in Siefert's first season calling the shots.
"There's a lot of things you have to deal with that aren't football-related, which are fine, you just have a lot of things you got to take care of," Siefert said of becoming a head coach.
Though his role may be slightly different now, he still leans on the fundamentals.
"The things that I felt like I've learned through the years of being a coach are still the things that work. Sometimes staying simple are the things that work," he said.
"We know we're going to work hard at practice," Salt Fork fullback/linebacker Jamison Chambliss said. "We know we're going to be a physical team and kind of push the weight room a lot and really just trying to perfect everything we do at practice."
The Storm start the season with back-to-back road games at Clifton Central and Westville, before a week three home opener against Hoopeston.
